author: Marina Sorochan
text:
Hi! Someone took my green satin beddings from the A6A laundry. Please return them as soon as possible. Security already knows about the situation, but honestly, it’s not the first time something is literally STOLEN from the laundry in this university, so I think referring to police can work even better.

Additionally, due to the absence of cameras in laundry rooms, people let themselves do stuff that they would never do if their face was recorded. I have encountered how people throw away my clothes from the washing machine before the cycle has even started and wash their clothes instead using my detergent. Or put their clothes on top of mine in the dryer, or just switching off the washing machine in the middle of the cycle and throwing my clothes to the basket (basket is the best case scenario here).

Don’t you think the situation would change if people knew they are being recorded? Maybe we should think about asking the uni to install cameras to laundry rooms at least in visitation buildings. Thus they can be directly punished without all the steps that I am going through now. Stealing is a crime in every universe, in every country and in every institution. If you think that you can steal 200$ beddings from a room without cameras and not face punishment, you are deeply mistaken. It’s just a question of time for how long me and other people who have encountered such an unethical behaviour will be patient. And is there really a room for such behaviour at such a university? 

Not a threat, but if the beddings are not returned up to the end of this week, I will contact the police and maybe then you will stop doing such disgusting stuff!

author: Aleksandrina Dimova
text:
**PARTICIPANTS NEEDED FOR A PSYCHOLOGY STUDY**

**Earn up to 450 AED in Gratitude Vouchers (e.g., Amazon gift cards)!**

 

Hi, everyone!

 

The Sreenivasan Lab is conducting a research study for a project examining how hormones influence memory across the menstrual cycle. We are looking for female participants with regular cycles who are interested in contributing to research in women's health.

 

**What you’ll be asked to do:**
* Fill out a form that will ask questions to determine initial eligibility
* If eligible based on the questions, provide a blood sample for genetic testing (COMT gene)
* If you meet the genetic criteria, track your menstrual cycle using an app (Euki) and at-home LH urine-based test strips
* If eligible based on cycle tracking, complete two memory experiments (each ~90 minutes), scheduled during different hormonal phases of your cycl
* Submit two venous blood samples for hormone analysis (estrogen, progesterone, LH)

 

Participants must be available to attend both required experimental sessions in-person.

 

Eligibility requirements will be shared via email with interested participants. We will ask for minimal information to determine your eligibility in the initial survey and will avoid collecting any details we do not need.

 

Here is a brief interest survey to get started: https://nyu.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_egqnu2mCNMgRXgy

author: Malika Singh
text:
## Crowdfunding for a Cross-Border Documentary by Two NYUAD Film Grads !
## 
## TLDR: Joint documentary film being made across India-Pakistan. Requesting you to come forward and fund it in whatever capacity you can. Please?

Hi folks, here’s a documentary project that Ibad Hassan and I have been working on since December. 

**https://seermeinmanikmotilal.com/ **

**^**find here the **trailer, photographs, and a published report **for The Polis Project that we authored a few months ago

The film is a story of **fisherfolk families who often get detained** near a disputed region between the ever-hostile states of India and Pakistan.

From fishing villages of Karachi to the settlements of southern Gujarat, we want to explore a shared reality from both sides; of navigating day-to-day lives in the absence of loved ones, fishing in dying coasts, and fishermen seeking long voyages in the Arabian Sea despite endless risk. 

This film has also been a way for us to collaborate while our states remain eerily silent over everyday violences imposed on everyday people.  

In English, the film transliterates to ***where did the pearls go?****,* and is sort of an ode to all that once traversed the depths of the Arabian Sea. 

**TO HELP FUND US, GO TO THE BOTTOM OF THE WEBSITE AND PAY WHATEVER YOU CAN !**

**PLEASE TAG PEOPLE BELOW !**

Any contribution, big or small, goes a long way especially in our parts of the world (think USD to PKR ffs). If you too are broke like us, think of 3 people you could send this forward to, and then do so? Please? To all the drops that maketh a sea 

With love and solidarity,

Malika and Ibad

author: Cristina Isabelle Yu
text:
## Performance

Middle East Premiere
# **The Butterfly Who Flew Into The Rave - Oli Mathiesen with Lucy Lynch and Sharvon Mortimer**

Electrifying contemporary street dance

Thu - Sat, Sep 10 - 12 @ 7:30pm

Black Box | The Arts Center 

From Aotearoa (New Zealand), Oli Mathiesen with Lucy Lynch and Sharvon Mortimer perform the award-winning *The Butterfly Who Flew Into The Rave*, an endurance-based dance work set to the booming Detroit techno album Nocturbulous Behaviour by Suburban Knight.

Exploring the movement vocabulary used in techno through the atmosphere and culture of a three-day rave condensed into an hour. Witness the relentless movement of three bodies, seamless without pause, and detailed down to every beat. Indulge in the pain, sweat, and cathartic mess; a display of pure endurance to achieve a goal. *The Butterfly Who Flew Into The Rave *is a spectacle of the human body as a victim to music,  passion, and our endless desire to achieve more: To win and win again.

After the performance, you’ll be invited to dance on stage in The Black Box to guest DJs at our very own techno-fueled Raving Ovation powered by Analog Room, included in your ticket price. Featured DJs include Moe on Thursday, Cyrill Reaidy on Friday, and Bazzzuk on Saturday.

Use code: **arts4students** to book your FREE ticket [https://publicprograms.nyuad.nyu.edu/en/the-arts-center/events/2026/september/the-butterfly-who-flew-into-the-rave.html](https://publicprograms.nyuad.nyu.edu/en/the-arts-center/events/2026/september/the-butterfly-who-flew-into-the-rave.html)

The Social Sciences Committee is gathering student feedback to explore introducing a **Migration Studies Minor** at NYUAD! 

Global mobility, border politics, and human displacement shape so much of today’s world, and our academic options should reflect that. **CALLING ALL ASPIRING EDITORS AND SOCIAL SCIENCE ENTHUSIASTS**

The NYUAD Journal of Social Sciences is currently looking for Junior Editors!

**Job Description:**

Junior Editors will commit four full semesters—two as Junior Editors and two as Senior Editors. Junior Editors do not need to be in Abu Dhabi for Fall 2026 or Spring 2027 to be eligible. As Junior Editors, students will participate in the production of the JSS. Their responsibilities will include copy-editing, source checking, LaTeX formatting, student outreach, and participation in the editorial process.

This opportunity is ideal for candidates who are considering graduate school studies, publications, or research-related careers in the social sciences. The ideal candidate should be interested in reading and producing student research. author: Dmitrij Fleming
text:
❌ There’s a common MYTH that eating eggs or meat every day is automatically bad for your health and will raise your cholesterol

But it’s not that simple.

The important thing is not just whether you eat eggs or meat, but how much saturated fat you consume throughout the entire day 👆🏻

A high intake of saturated fat can contribute to higher LDL (“bad”) cholesterol. 

But if you have eggs for breakfast and then choose mostly unsaturated fats for the rest of the day — such as olive oil, nuts, avocado and other plant-based sources — you can still have a healthy, balanced diet ✅

Personally, I eat eggs every morning and simply pay attention to the overall balance of my diet.

👉 Don’t blame one food. Look at the whole picture.

It’s your overall daily diet that matters, not the fact that you ate a few eggs.

#diet #health #healthyfood #fatloss

author: 360º  VR Photography - 360pano.eu
text:
Fallen Icarus At The Temple Of Concordia

🔍 HD version: https://www.360cities.net/image/fallen-icarus-at-the-temple-of-concordia

The Temple of Concordia stands in the Valley of the Temples at Agrigento, Sicily, on the site of the ancient Greek city of Akragas. Built around 440–430 BC, it is one of the finest and best-preserved examples of Doric architecture. Its exceptional state of preservation is partly due to its conversion into a Christian church in late antiquity. In front of the temple lies Icaro Caduto (Fallen Icarus), a monumental bronze sculpture by Polish artist Igor Mitoraj, donated to the archaeological park in 2011. Inspired by the Greek myth of Icarus, the fallen figure creates a striking contrast between contemporary sculpture and the monumental architecture of the ancient world.

author: Jake Boys
text:
In the early 1970s, Joyce McKinney, a former Miss Wyoming winner and cheerleader from North Carolina, met and fell deeply in love with Kirk Anderson, a young man belonging to the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

When Anderson suddenly disappeared to serve his Mormon mission in England, McKinney became obsessed with tracking him down.

In September 1977, McKinney traveled to England accompanied by a male friend named Keith May.

She ambushed Anderson outside an LDS church meetinghouse in Ewell, Surrey, allegedly dr*gging him with chlorof*rm and taking him at g*npoint.

They drove Anderson to a rented, remote 17th-century cottage in Okehampton, Devon.

Anderson was chained to a bed with mink-lined handcuffs and forced to repeatedly have s*x with McKinney over three days, as she was desperate to bear his child.

Eventually, Anderson escaped and immediately went to the British police.

McKinney and May were quickly arrested and charged with false imprisonment and possession of an imitation firearm.

Under English law at the time, a woman could not legally be charged with the r*pe of a man.

Before the case could go to trial, McKinney and May skipped bail.

They managed to flee England and return to the United States, reportedly disguised as mime artists and utilizing fake passports.

Because British authorities chose not to seek extradition, they were never tried for the alleged kidnapping.

Seven years after the British scandal, McKinney was arrested in Salt Lake City, Utah, outside Anderson's workplace.

Police found maps, photos of Anderson's house, rope, and handcuffs in her possession.

She was charged with disturbing the peace and stalking, though she claimed she was merely researching the ending to a book.

In her later years, McKinney fell into severe hardship and became homeless, living out of her car.

In 2019, she was charged with hit-and-run mansla*ghter after striking a 91-year-old pedestrian in California.

The courts eventually found her mentally incompetent to stand trial, resulting in her permanent placement in a psychiatric facility, where she remains today.
